The interpretation for this statistic is that the data values in Group #1 are about 4.1 points away from the
mean, on average. That isn’t quite correct due to the order of operations of the process, but that is how
we interpret the standard deviation. (The actual average deviation using the absolute value is
approximately 3.8, so the process we used gives us a very similar number, 4.1, with the advantage that
the new idea has wider applications.)

standard deviation comes out to , or 2.6 rounded to one decimal place.

Before we cover formulas and technology, we can summarize how we will interpret standard deviation.
Important Point! What does Standard Deviation tell us?
Whether we are working with populations or samples, we interpret standard deviation as a measure
1. Standard deviation gives an idea of how close the data are to the mean, or how “spread-out” the
2. Most of the data will be within one standard deviation of the mean.
3. LARGER standard deviations correspond to more widely dispersed or spread-out data. More
variation indicates a larger standard deviation. A SMALL standard deviation corresponds to
data that is less dispersed, less variable, and more closely grouped. See
